Photograph: Axel Schmidt/Reuters View image in fullscreen The bomb attached to the drone did not detonate, due to a faulty detonator. Photograph: Axel Schmidt/Reuters Germany Analysis The Leipzig drone bomb marks a dangerous escalation for Europe Dan Sabbagh Defence and security editor Initial evidence suggests aerial drone, found near Ukrainian cargo planes at German airport, came from Russia Wed 5 Aug 2026 13.32 EDT Last modified on Wed 5 Aug 2026 14.53 EDT Share The armed drone found at Leipzig airport on Wednesday may not have exploded, but the fact that it got inside the perimeter, close to Ukrainian cargo planes , raises obvious concerns for the security of international aviation. Though the identity of the culprits is unknown, the initial evidence points firmly towards a Russian-orchestrated plot. It is the first time that a drone with explosives has been found in Europe far from the Ukrainian border. Photographs published by German newspapers show a quadcopter, a design familiar from the Ukraine war, with a package attached.
